sections.markdown:
## C — Examinations (Section 6)

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
The written knowledge test samples handbook material to confirm basic grasp of Utah law and safe driving habits [A01].
Why it matters: study the handbook itself.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test is untimed and typically takes 30 to 45 minutes, with passing set at 80 percent or better [A01].
Why it matters: no clock pressure, but the cutoff is fixed.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
A candidate may take two knowledge tests in one day when the Division can accommodate them, and a failed attempt needs a scheduled retest visit [A01].
Why it matters: plan same-day retry versus return trip.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
One fee covers up to three knowledge-test attempts within 12 months, and after three failures another fee buys three more attempts [A01].
Why it matters: the core attempt-limit and fee rule.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
First-time Class D applicants must also pass a Traffic Safety and Trends exam with a 100 percent score, taken online as often as needed before licensing [A01].
Why it matters: a second perfect-score requirement surprises many.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Half the Safety and Trends questions cover major causes of traffic death drawn from Utah Highway Safety Office statistics [A01].
Why it matters: prioritize fatal-crash causes for that exam.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A02
The skills test requires a properly registered, safe vehicle with working belts, and only applicant plus examiner may ride along [A02].
Why it matters: vehicle or passenger errors force rescheduling.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A02
The minimum skills-test age is 16 years at the DLD and 15 years with a Third-Party Tester or high school [A02].
Why it matters: age path depends on test provider.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A80
Scored skills include attitude, technique, posture and lane use, turns, starts and stops, hill and parallel parking, signs and signals, backing, U-turns, steering, intersections, lane changes, and safe operation [A80][S80_0].
Why it matters: the full maneuver checklist to practice.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A81
A failed skills test needs more practice first, allows only one skills test per day with possible waits, needs another fee after three failures, and all tests must finish within six months of paying [A81].
Why it matters: pacing, fee, and deadline limits combined.
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A03
The test vehicle needs current rear-plate registration, front and rear signals plus brake lights, horn, sound tires, firm brakes, opening driver window, clear windshield, two mirrors with a left-outside mirror, doors opening inside and out, fixed passenger seat, belts, and parking brake [A03].
Why it matters: every item can trigger a reschedule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A04
Automatic skills-test failure follows a moving citation or ignored law, missed yield, avoidable contact, forcing evasive action, needless curb or sidewalk contact, examiner takeover, or driving much too fast or too slow [A04].
Why it matters: the fail-on-sight list to memorize cold.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0035]

High-yield ranked: 1) pass scores 80 and 100 percent, 2) attempt and fee caps, 3) automatic failures, 4) vehicle checklist [A01].
Misconceptions: the knowledge test is timed; three failures end the process; any friend may ride along [A02].
Mnemonics: 80-100 rule pairs 80 percent knowledge pass with 100 percent trends pass [A01].
Glossary: DLD is the Driver License Division; Third-Party Tester is a certified outside examiner; trends exam is the online safety supplement [A02].
Dynamic facts isolated: scheduling site addresses and fee sums can change; verify current site and fees before visiting [A03].
